title: Restore Context Runtime First End-to-End Slice Verified
summary: The first complete Naya Power continuity slice is implemented and verified: Restore Context reconstructs current or historical state from repository reality, canonical state, and temporally valid Smart Notes, with checkpoint and handoff contracts and CI enforcement.
what_happened: The architectural review was converted into a working Restore Context runtime, acceptance tests, CI enforcement, canonical repository boot corrections, and governance guardrails.
what_we_learned: The smallest coherent vertical slice is more valuable than expanding the specification.
Temporal restore requires Git history in CI; shallow checkout is insufficient for historical verification.
Tests that write checkpoints into the repository can contaminate repository-reality evidence and must be isolated.
Governance guardrails must validate the actual current context rather than a stale hard-coded repository state.
why_it_matters: This establishes a real, model-independent continuity primitive instead of a documentation-only promise and creates a foundation for later retrieval, Oscar, learning, and self-optimization capabilities.
what_changed: Added current and historical restore modes.
Extended CI to execute and verify restore behavior.
Corrected the canonical repository/boot protocol from stale MaxRESULTS references.
Upgraded the context manifest to v4 and aligned its governance guardrail.
Changed the governance workflow to validate the actual PR context.
next_best_action: Merge only after the PR evidence remains green, then update canonical runtime state to record Restore Context as VERIFIED and begin the next vertical slice: evidence/claim enforcement plus adversarial tests.
